# FoodGauge

> FoodGauge is a free Android and iOS app that photographs a packaged food label, reads the printed ingredients and nutrition table with AI, and converts them into a single deterministic score from 1 to 5, together with the reasoning behind that score. It requires no barcode, no product database, and no user account.

Site: https://teach-bot-sys.github.io/foodgauge-site/
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/food.gauge/
Contact: mrfatihkrkmz@gmail.com
Publisher: Kaira Labs
Platforms: Android, iOS
Price: Free. No in-app purchases, no subscription.
App interface languages: English, Turkish (Russian and Arabic planned)
Site languages: English, Turkish, Russian, Arabic

## What makes FoodGauge different

Most food scanning apps read a barcode and look the product up in a central database. If the product is not in that database the user gets "product not found". This happens constantly with local brands, small producers, imported goods that never entered the catalogue, damaged barcodes, and bakery or deli items.

FoodGauge does not use barcodes and does not query a product database. It reads the printed label directly from a photo. There is therefore no catalogue for a product to be missing from.

## How the score is calculated

The AI component only extracts what is visible on the label. The score itself is produced by a deterministic rule engine, so the same label always yields the same number.

finalScore = nutritionQuality x 0.40 + processingIntensity x 0.35 + additiveRisk x 0.25

- Nutrition quality (40%): derived from the visible nutrition table — sugar, salt, fat, saturated fat, energy.
- Processing intensity (35%): additive-like signals in the ingredient list plus an estimate of how processed the product is.
- Additive risk (25%): evaluated against FoodGauge's own static additive rule set. FoodGauge does not claim any live lookup against EFSA, FDA, OpenFoodTox or Open Food Facts.

Override rule: if a high-risk additive, high-fructose corn syrup, or trans fat appears on the label, the final score is capped at 2.0 regardless of the other three signals.

Result labels: Good Choice, Use with Caution, Weak Choice, Unclear.
Turkish equivalents: İyi Seçim, Dikkatli, Zayıf Seçim, Belirsiz.
FoodGauge never labels a product "healthy" or "unhealthy".

## Added sugar vs total sugar

The nutrition table figure for "sugars" is total sugar. It includes sugar naturally present in fruit or milk. Added sugar can only be identified from the ingredient list. FoodGauge therefore reads added sugar from the ingredient list and treats the nutrition table as context. A "no added sugar" claim on the front of a pack is not sufficient on its own; the ingredient list decides.

## Unreadable labels

FoodGauge does not guess. If a photo cannot be read reliably, the result is marked Unclear and the user is asked to retake the photo. Unreadable scans are not saved to history. Ingredients and nutrition values are never invented.

## Privacy

- No account, registration, or personal profile.
- The camera is used only after the user chooses to take a photo. The photo picker passes only the single selected image.
- A compressed copy of the label image is sent to the analysis backend so the label can be read. It is not retained in the local history.
- Raw images, base64 payloads, and image file paths are never written to local history.
- Scan summaries and details are stored on the device only and can be deleted individually or cleared entirely.
- The app shows ads; ad personalisation follows the consent choice made on first launch, which can be revisited from the privacy screen.
- No medical profile, diet profile, or health record is created or requested.

## Important limitations

FoodGauge is not a medical, diagnostic, treatment, allergy-safety, diet, or calorie-counting application. It provides general information based only on what is visible on a food label. It makes no health claims about any product and its score is not a judgement about whether a food is healthy or safe for any individual. FoodGauge does not use Nutri-Score branding and is not affiliated with any food authority or product database.
